scores.claim_text: In January 2024 Reddit entered into certain data licensing arrangements with an aggregate transaction price of $203.0 million, a minimum of $66.4 million of which is expected to be recognized as revenue in 2024.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext on Alphabet/Google (CIK 0001652044) for 'Reddit' and broad full-text search for 'Reddit data', both pre-2024-03-21
scores.M_value: Alphabet filings: 0 hits for 'Reddit'; broad FTS 'Reddit data': 0 hits
scores.interpretation: The data-licensing counterparty is NOT named in Reddit's own prospectus (referred to only as 'certain data licensing arrangements'). A buyer purchasing a ~$200M multi-year data license is not a customer-concentration relationship the buyer must separately disclose, and $66.4M of 2024 data-licensing revenue is ~8% of total revenue (below the 10% customer-disclosure threshold Reddit itself affirms no customer exceeds). Per CALIBRATION heuristic 5/8, 0 counterparty mentions here is expected, not a contradiction. No federal registry covers a SaaS/data-licensing contract. Honestly UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: Reddit's content is a foundational part of how many of the leading large language models have been trained, and Reddit expects its data advantage to remain a key element in training future LLMs.
scores.M_check: megacap_namecheck on Alphabet/Microsoft/Amazon and edgar_fts on Alphabet for 'Reddit', pre-2024-03-21
scores.M_value: megacap_namecheck signal=INFLATION_SUSPECT (0 hits across Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon); Alphabet 10-K/10-Q: 0 'Reddit' mentions
scores.interpretation: The raw signal is INFLATION_SUSPECT, but this is a generic-marketing claim about the AI ecosystem's use of public web data, not a named operating contract. AI labs do not disclose individual training-data sources in SEC filings, so megacap-side silence is the expected baseline for ANY web-data provider and is not probative of inflation here (CALIBRATION heuristic 5/8 — counterparty would not separately disclose). No registry can confirm or refute which LLMs trained on Reddit data. UNVERIFIABLE rather than SEVERE; the INFLATION_SUSPECT label is a sector-mismatch false positive.

scores.claim_text: Reddit's revenue grew to $804.0 million in 2023 from $666.7 million in 2022, generated substantially all from advertising, with no single customer accounting for more than 10% of revenue in 2022 or 2023.
scores.M_check: No external registry covers self-serve/managed advertising revenue or customer concentration for a social platform
scores.interpretation: Pure financial-statement / accounting claim (audited revenue, gross margin, customer-concentration disclosure). No federal registry (EPA/USAspending/USPTO/FDA/CT.gov) covers advertising revenue. Per EXTRACT RUBRIC this is low-discriminative accounting; recorded for completeness and scored honestly UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: Reddit's data advantage and intellectual property are a key competitive asset, and the Revolving Credit Facility is secured by liens on substantially all assets including intellectual property assets.
scores.M_value: n_total_applications=2, n_granted (pre-cutoff)=1; only filing is a single provisional/non-provisional pair titled 'Decentralized Social-Media Platform'
scores.interpretation: USPTO shows an essentially empty patent portfolio at the IPO date. However, Reddit's IP claim is explicitly grounded in its DATA CORPUS and trademarks, not a patent estate — the prospectus never asserts a large patent count, so this is NOT the Nikola pattern (CALIBRATION heuristic 7). The thin patent count is a mild gap between the marketed 'intellectual property' framing and registry-recordable IP, but is fully consistent with a content platform whose moat is data, not patents. Scored MODERATE (ceiling-vs-implied gap), not SEVERE.

scores.claim_text: Reddit is committed under non-cancellable cloud agreements (Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud Platform) to spend at least $385.0 million through September 2026.
scores.interpretation: AWS/GCP are vendors TO Reddit; a cloud provider does not separately disclose an individual customer of this size in its filings (Reddit is the buyer, not a >10% customer of Amazon). The purchase commitment is disclosed in Reddit's own audited contractual-obligations note ($338.2M table / $385M through Sept 2026). 0 megacap-side mentions is expected and non-probative. UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: Reddit had an average of 73.1 million DAUq and 267.5 million WAUq in the three months ended December 31, 2023.
scores.M_check: No external registry records a social platform's daily/weekly active-user metrics
scores.interpretation: Self-reported usage metrics (DAUq/WAUq) are not captured by any federal registry or counterparty filing. Per CALIBRATION heuristic 8, platform engagement metrics are inherently UNVERIFIABLE from independent registries; do not manufacture severity.

scores.claim_text: As of December 31, 2023 Reddit had $1.2 billion in cash and marketable securities and believes its liquidity plus the $750.0M Revolving Credit Facility is sufficient for at least the next 12 months (no going-concern doubt).
scores.interpretation: Detector finds no going-concern language, corroborating the prospectus's own clean disclosure. At the IPO date the prospectus shows $1.2B liquidity, $804M revenue at 84% gross margin, and modest operating cash burn (~$75M in 2023) — fully consistent with no substantial-doubt condition. This honest financial-health disclosure is independently corroborated. PASS.
